fixed_statement:
Let \(k\ge 1\) be an integer.
Let \(J_1,\ldots,J_m\) be mutually independent and uniform on \(\{1,\dots,k\}\).
Set \(v_i^{(J_i)}=1\), and set \(v_i^{(j)}=0\) for all \(j\neq J_i\).
Define \(X^{(j)}=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i v_i^{(j)}\).
The \(k\) identically distributed random variables \(X^{(j)}\) sum to exactly \(1\).
Let \(A_j\) be the event that \(X^{(j)}\ge 1/k\).

\[
\Pr[A_1]\ge \frac{1}{k}.
\]
fixed_proof:
At least one of them must evaluate to \(1/k\) or greater. Therefore
\[
\Pr\Big[\bigcup_{j=1}^k A_j\Big]=1.
\]
By the union bound,
\[
1
=
\Pr\Big[\bigcup_{j=1}^k A_j\Big]
\le
\sum_{j=1}^k \Pr[A_j]
=
k\Pr[A_1].
\]
Dividing by \(k\) gives \(\Pr[A_1]\ge 1/k\).
